original_query: select    min(s_store_name)   ,min(s_company_id)   ,min(s_street_number)   ,min(s_street_name)   ,min(s_suite_number)   ,min(s_city)   ,min(s_zip)   ,min(ss_ticket_number)   ,min(ss_sold_date_sk)   ,min(sr_returned_date_sk)   ,min(ss_item_sk)   ,min(d1.d_date_sk) from    store_sales   ,store_returns   ,store   ,date_dim d1   ,date_dim d2 where     d2.d_moy = 8 and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk and ss_sold_date_sk   = d1.d_date_sk and sr_returned_date_sk   = d2.d_date_sk and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk and ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and sr_store_sk = s_store_sk and d1.d_date between (d2.d_date - interval '120' day)                and d2.d_date and d1.d_dow = 5 and s_state in ('IN','NM','VA')  ;
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    MIN(s.s_store_name)      AS s_store_name,
    MIN(s.s_company_id)      AS s_company_id,
    MIN(s.s_street_number)   AS s_street_number,
    MIN(s.s_street_name)     AS s_street_name,
    MIN(s.s_suite_number)    AS s_suite_number,
    MIN(s.s_city)            AS s_city,
    MIN(s.s_zip)             AS s_zip,
    MIN(ss.ss_ticket_number) AS ss_ticket_number,
    MIN(ss.ss_sold_date_sk)  AS ss_sold_date_sk,
    MIN(sr.sr_returned_date_sk) AS sr_returned_date_sk,
    MIN(ss.ss_item_sk)       AS ss_item_sk,
    MIN(d1.d_date_sk)        AS d_date_sk
FROM date_dim d2
JOIN store_returns sr
  ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
JOIN store_sales ss
  ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
 AND ss.ss_item_sk       = sr.sr_item_sk
 AND ss.ss_customer_sk   = sr.sr_customer_sk
 AND ss.ss_store_sk      = sr.sr_store_sk
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
 AND s.s_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
 AND d1.d_dow = 5
 AND d1.d_date BETWEEN d2.d_date - INTERVAL '120 days' AND d2.d_date
WHERE d2.d_moy = 8
  AND s.s_state IN ('IN','NM','VA');

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Converted implicit comma-style joins into explicit ANSI JOINs with all join keys in ON clauses. Added the transitive predicate ss.ss_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk explicitly in the store_sales/store_returns join so the optimizer can use it directly when joining the fact tables, rather than relying only on transitive closure through the store table.

Reordered the FROM clause to start from the filtered date_dim d2 (d_moy = 8), which reduces store_returns to roughly 1/12 of its 7.2M rows (~600K) before joining the 28.8M-row store_sales table. This drives the join with the more selective side first.

Pushed dimension filters (d1.d_dow = 5, d2.d_moy = 8, s.s_state IN (...)) into JOIN conditions / WHERE so they are applied as early as possible. Rewrote the interval expression as d2.d_date - INTERVAL '120 days' for standard syntax.

No CTEs introduced: date_dim filters are simple single-table predicates that the optimizer can push down inline; materializing them would add overhead without benefit given there are no repeated subquery computations.

The 120-day interval constant is expressed directly in the join predicate; no further foldable constants exist. The MIN() single-row aggregate is preserved as-is since individual MIN values may originate from different joined rows.
